content.comment_body: Has anyone else experienced this issue? I've checked the forum and available advice but haven't found a solution. I'm running [product_name] Demo version [version_no] on Windows XP, both are fully updated. My computer is a Pentium processor with support for two monitors. When I attempt to start [product_name], the program crashes within seconds, but the operating system continues running. If I disable the secondary monitor, [product_name] starts and operates normally. Enabling the second monitor after launching the software doesn't cause any issues. I had this crash issue with an earlier version too. I'm not sure if this problem is unique to my hardware setup or common with dual monitor configurations. Any thoughts? I can provide further hardware details if needed.

Hello, I use a laptop with an additional monitor and haven't experienced issues. My operating system is Windows XP Pro SP2, and I utilize the extended desktop feature. It could be a graphics card driver issue. Have you tried installing the latest driver for your card? Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Thanks for the fast response. Since you're using extended desktop on XP SP2 without issues, this likely points to a hardware issue on my end. I've already updated drivers for both video cards—one Radeon and one NVIDIA—yet the issue persists. For clarification, my processor is a Pentium 4. I plan to test [product_name] soon on another dual monitor system and will share the results. Is it possible this is a limitation of the Demo version?
Hello, I'm using Windows XP Pro SP3 with two monitors (21.5" and 20.5") and haven't had any problems. You might want to update your Java installation.

Everyone, Good suggestion, [user_name]. I tried updating Java since it's caused issues for others, but it didn't help. There seemed to be some confusion during the update, so maybe it wasn't completed successfully. I also tested [product_name] [version_no] using the same installation file on another system—a Pentium D running XP SP2 with dual monitors. On that setup, it worked without problems. The main difference is that the other system has a single motherboard graphics card, not two. This confirms it's not a general issue but specific to my hardware configuration. I have a temporary workaround and will share a real solution if I identify the problem or fix it.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but are you using two VGA cards—one external (AGP/PCI) and one internal (on the motherboard)—with each connected to its own monitor? If so, encountering problems is to be expected. Try connecting both monitors to one graphics card (using extended desktop settings) or disable the internal card.

analysis.insight_summary: The software [product_name] ([version_no] Demo and previous version) experiences crashes on Windows XP when used with dual monitors connected to different graphics cards. Users found that disabling the secondary monitor allows the program to start, after which monitors can be enabled without issue. This points to a compatibility flaw in handling systems with multiple GPUs and monitors, and the software does not notify users of this limitation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to start and function correctly in dual monitor setups on Windows XP, regardless of the number or type of graphics cards present.
